items.title: The Reply-All Apocalypse
items.premise: An employee accidentally hits 'Reply-All' to a company-wide email asking 'Who ate my donut?' and watches in horror as executives join the thread to debate corporate pastry ethics. The punchline: the CEO admits he ate it, but still writes 'Let's take this offline' to the entire company.

items.title: The Out-of-Office Escape Room
items.premise: Just as an employee is about to log off for a long weekend, the boss drops a 'quick 5-minute task' that turns into a multi-hour corporate labyrinth. The punchline: the employee successfully escapes the building at 5:01 PM, only to receive a calendar invite for a Monday 6 AM alignment meeting.

items.title: The Tupperware Criminal Investigation
items.premise: Mom interrogates the entire household because a high-value, stain-resistant Tupperware container has gone missing. The punchline: Dad is found using it as a makeshift tackle box in the garage, complete with fishing hooks resting inside a container meant for leftover pasta.

items.title: Grandma's Wi-Fi Password Mastery
items.premise: Grandma tries to guess the ultra-secure Wi-Fi password by suggesting ancient proverbs and her wedding anniversary instead of looking at the router sticker. The punchline: she guesses it on the first try because the password is literally her own legendary cooking recipe.

items.title: The Icebreaker Backfire
items.premise: On a first date, a guy tries an advanced psychological icebreaker question about 'core trauma' to sound deep and mysterious. The punchline: the date reveals her core trauma is people who ask advanced psychological icebreaker questions on first dates, and she instantly venmos him half the coffee bill.

items.title: Third-Wheeling Extreme Edition
items.premise: A best friend tags along on a romantic picnic just to 'protect the vibe' but ends up acting like a third-wheel film critic grading the couple's conversation. The punchline: the couple gets so annoyed they break up, leaving the best friend and the ex-date to bond over shared snacks.

items.title: The Group Chat Ghost Town
items.premise: A student frantically texts the group project chat at 3 AM asking who is doing the final presentation slides due in four hours. The punchline: everyone replies simultaneously with identical screenshots of blank templates, and they end up presenting a history of memes instead.

items.title: The High-Stakes Pen Exchange
items.premise: During a surprise pop quiz, a student desperately begs a classmate to lend them a working pen like it's an illegal black-market arms deal.The punchline: the pen runs out of ink on the very first letter of their name, forcing them to finish the exam using sheer finger sweat and pencil dust.

items.title: The Gym Membership Houdini
items.premise: A broke guy tries every loophole imaginable to cancel an annual gym membership without paying the ridiculous cancellation fee. The punchline: he actually succeeds by legally changing his name and moving to a new apartment, only to realize the gym opened a new branch right next door.

items.title: The Microwave Masterclass Budget
items.premise: A frugal roommate tries to teach the others how to meal prep gourmet meals using only a single microwave and a dream. The punchline: the meal explodes, costing triple the grocery budget in cleaning supplies, proving that sometimes eating instant noodles is cheaper.

items.title: The Accidental Blessing Swap
items.premise: A person tries to secretly pay for a stranger's expensive grocery basket to do a good deed of the day, but grabs the wrong cart. The punchline: the stranger turns out to be a coupon wizard who actually paid for 200 items for less than three dollars, leaving our hero deeply confused.

items.title: The Apology Marathon
items.premise: After accidentally breaking a neighbor's tiny garden gnome, a guy overcomplicates a simple apology by building an entire mini-colosseum as compensation. The punchline: the neighbor reveals they hated that specific gnome because it looked like their ex-mother-in-law.
